quick: 5 mg PO three times daily before meals
Use with caution in hepatic impairment
LFTs if prolonged use; symptom response
summary: Mosapride is a selective 5-HT4 receptor agonist prokinetic used to relieve gastrointestinal symptoms associated with chronic gastritis and functional dyspepsia, such as heartburn, nausea and early satiety. Usual adult dose is 5 mg three times daily before meals. Unlike cisapride, it has minimal effect on cardiac QT interval. Not FDA-approved.
indications: Gastrointestinal symptoms (heartburn, nausea, vomiting) associated with chronic gastritis
Improvement of upper GI motility / delayed gastric emptying

dosage.n: Citrate salt; reassess if no benefit after 2 weeks

admin: Take orally three times daily, typically before meals
Reassess therapy if symptoms do not improve within 2 weeks
Discontinue if no clinical benefit is obtained
moa: Mosapride is a selective agonist at serotonin 5-HT4 receptors on enteric cholinergic neurons. Activation enhances acetylcholine release in the myenteric plexus, increasing upper gastrointestinal motility and accelerating gastric emptying. It has little or no affinity for dopamine D2 or cardiac hERG/5-HT3 receptors, so extrapyramidal and significant QT effects are uncommon.

absolute: Conditions where increased GI motility could be harmful (GI hemorrhage, mechanical obstruction or perforation)

preg: Safety in pregnancy has not been established. Avoid unless the potential benefit clearly outweighs the risk; use the lowest effective dose if treatment is essential.
lact: Excretion into human milk is not adequately characterized. Avoid use during breastfeeding or discontinue nursing; animal data suggest excretion into milk.
renal: Limited pharmacokinetic data in renal impairment; use with caution and consider the lowest effective dose, monitoring for accumulation and effect.
hepatic: Mosapride is metabolized mainly by hepatic CYP3A4; use with caution in hepatic impairment and monitor liver function with prolonged use.

moderate: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (erythromycin, clarithromycin, azole antifungals) - may increase mosapride exposure
Anticholinergic agents - may antagonize prokinetic effect
minor: Drugs whose absorption depends on gastric transit - altered absorption due to faster emptying
interactions.food: Usually taken before meals; food may modestly affect onset.
interactions.alcohol: No specific clinically significant interaction reported; moderate intake.
interactions.diagnostics: Rare transient elevations in liver enzymes reported.

monitoring: Symptom response within 2 weeks; discontinue if ineffective
Liver function tests with prolonged therapy
counsel: Take before meals three times a day as prescribed
Report persistent diarrhea or abdominal pain
Stop and seek care if yellowing of skin/eyes or dark urine occurs
Inform the doctor if symptoms do not improve within about 2 weeks
pk: Store at room temperature, protected from moisture and light
pearls: Not FDA-approved; widely used in Asia (SmPC/regional labeling) - this record is based on EMA-region SmPC and standard references rather than an FDA label
Preferred over cisapride because it lacks clinically significant QT prolongation
Lacks dopamine D2 antagonism, so extrapyramidal effects and hyperprolactinemia are uncommon (unlike metoclopramide/domperidone)
Active metabolite des-mosapride also has 5-HT4 activity
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered. If it is nearly time for the next dose, skip it and resume the usual schedule; do not double up.
overdose: Experience with overdose is limited. Manage symptomatically and supportively; treat excessive GI effects (diarrhea, cramping) with fluid and electrolyte support. There is no specific antidote.
